# References · Tools and tests

> The ideas behind the test harness, the mutation checks and the sanitizers used across this repo.

5 works · difficulty: ★☆☆ accessible · ★★☆ technical · ★★★ research-grade  
Read with the [three-pass method](../docs/papers.md#how-to-read-a-paper). Every link is a Google Scholar search for the exact title. [Master index →](../docs/papers.md)

## Testing as a discipline

#### ★★☆ QuickCheck: a lightweight tool for random testing of Haskell programs

Claessen & Hughes · 2000 · *ICFP* · paper · [Scholar ↗](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=%22QuickCheck%3A%20a%20lightweight%20tool%20for%20random%20testing%20of%20Haskell%20programs%22)

- **Why:** Property-based testing: state invariants and test them on random inputs. The Mark XI tests (`log(exp(ξ)) = ξ` for 10k random twists) are exactly this.
- **Read:** Sections 1–3.

#### ★★☆ Hints on test data selection: Help for the practicing programmer

DeMillo, Lipton & Sayward · 1978 · *IEEE Computer* · paper · [Scholar ↗](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=%22Hints%20on%20test%20data%20selection%3A%20Help%20for%20the%20practicing%20programmer%22)

- **Why:** The origin of mutation testing: plant a bug and check that your tests catch it. That's how every suite in this repo was validated.
- **Read:** All of it.

#### ★★☆ An analysis and survey of the development of mutation testing

Jia & Harman · 2011 · *IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering* · paper · [Scholar ↗](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=%22An%20analysis%20and%20survey%20of%20the%20development%20of%20mutation%20testing%22)

- **Why:** A survey of mutation testing: operators, equivalent mutants and the cost trade-offs.
- **Read:** Sections 1–3.

## Tools that find bugs for you

#### ★★☆ AddressSanitizer: A fast address sanity checker

Serebryany et al. · 2012 · *USENIX ATC* · paper · [Scholar ↗](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=%22AddressSanitizer%3A%20A%20fast%20address%20sanity%20checker%22)

- **Why:** How AddressSanitizer works: shadow memory and redzones. Behind `make SAN=1`.
- **Read:** Sections 1–3.

#### ★★★ CDSChecker: checking concurrent data structures written with C/C++ atomics

Norris & Demsky · 2013 · *OOPSLA* · paper · [Scholar ↗](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=%22CDSChecker%3A%20checking%20concurrent%20data%20structures%20written%20with%20C/C%2B%2B%20atomics%22)

- **Why:** Exhaustive exploration of C/C++11 atomic interleavings, the idea behind Rust's `loom` (Mark III).
- **Read:** The introduction and the algorithm overview.
